audit.whatIsWrong: Three chart rows contradict their own explanation text: whys[3] says levels 4-5 flip to you but win[3] is Swain; whys[4] says 6 swings back to Swain but win[4] is Skill; whys[5] says first item favours you but win[5] is Skill.
audit.why: The packet chart is [Swain, Swain, Swain, Dr. Mundo, Swain, Dr. Mundo, Skill], which matches the whys[] on all seven rows. The shape is right too: Swain owns the ranged phase, Mundo steals 4-5 once the Q slow and Heart Zapper are online, Demonic Ascension takes 6 back, and the first tank item plus tenacity flips it again.
audit.corrected: L1-L3 Swain, L4-5 Dr. Mundo, L6 Swain, first item Dr. Mundo, 2+ items Skill.

audit.whatIsWrong: Demonic Ascension's cooldown is printed as an em-dash — literally '(—)' — in breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].t, the two places the reader goes to find it.
audit.why: It is 120s at all ranks, 650 range, and Riot's text says the form 'is indefinite as long as Swain drains enemy champions'. That last clause is the spike: it is not a duration you wait out, it is a heal you have to cut. Your own Maximum Dosage is also 120s, so the two ults are on the same clock and whoever presses second usually wins.
audit.corrected: 120s written into both fields, with the indefinite-while-draining condition and the Grievous Wounds answer.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four fields state that Ravenous Flock is a percent-max-health effect that 'punishes your health-stacking'. It is not. Nevermove's actual mechanic — it roots on the RETURN, not the outgoing cast — is never stated, and Mundo's passive is never connected to it.
audit.why: Riot's text for Ravenous Flock: 'Swain's ravens collect Soul Fragments that heal him and permanently increase his maximum health.' The maximum health it raises is Swain's own. Nothing in it scales off your health bar. The kit file's percentHealth flag came from that sentence and misread whose health it meant. Nevermove: 'Swain launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits' — you dodge the return path, not the throw. And that root is an Immobilizing effect, so Goes Where He Pleases eats the first one and drops a cannister.
audit.corrected: whys[0], spikes[0].text, early and wants.foe[2] now describe the passive as Swain's own sustain and health growth. tradeGood and breakdown.cooldowns now carry the return-path root and the passive interaction.

audit.whatIsWrong: No usable cooldown appeared anywhere; the only one printed was blank.
audit.why: Death's Hand 7/6/5/4/3 at 750 range, Vision of Empire 22/21/20/19/18, Nevermove 12/11.5/11/10.5/10 at 850, Demonic Ascension 120s. Nevermove's 12s is the window you step into.
audit.corrected: Nevermove's 12s and Death's Hand's 750/7s now appear in breakdown.cooldowns, early and tradeGood.

audit.why: Spirit Visage and Mercury's Treads are right and report[8].t already names both. The supplied 'needs-antiheal' interaction is also correct — Ravenous Flock heals off Soul Fragments and Demonic Ascension is a sustained drain, so Grievous Wounds timing genuinely decides the extended fight, and that is now stated with the cooldown.

edits.after: His window: Demonic Ascension is also 120s and it does not expire while he drains you. Refuse the 6 all-in unless your R is already up.

notes:
REJECTED A SUPPLIED INTERACTION. missingInteractions offers: "Swain bypasses stacking resistances (Ravenous Flock (P)) — raw armour or MR is the wrong answer here." Ravenous Flock does not bypass resistances and does not scale off your health at all; Riot's text has it healing Swain and raising Swain's own maximum health. The kit's percentHealth flag misread whose maximum health the sentence refers to. The same false claim was already in four fields on the page and I corrected all four. The other supplied interaction (needs-antiheal) is correct and is now stated with the 120s cooldown.

Demonic Ascension's cooldown was rendered as '(—)' in both places it appears. It is 120s — the same as Maximum Dosage, which is the single most useful sequencing fact in this matchup.

Nevermove roots on the RETURN pass, not the outgoing cast. No field said so.
